title: Blueprint Builder Checkpoint
intro: A class is a blueprint, an object is a thing made from it, and inheritance lets one blueprint build on another. Eleven rounds across both lessons. Get them right on the first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.explain: class defines a new kind of thing. def defines a function or a method inside one.

options: It runs when an object is made and stores its starting values
It is the name of the class
rounds.explain: Python calls __init__ automatically the moment you create an object, which is why it is where the attributes get set.
"Rex" was passed in and stored on the object as self.name, so reading d.name gives it back.

rounds.prompt: Two objects, one class. What does the second line print?
rounds.explain: Every object keeps its own attributes. Making b did not touch a, and the two names never mix.

rounds.prompt: This method is missing something. Pick the fix.
rounds.explain: Python passes the object in as the first argument automatically, so the method has to have a parameter waiting for it.
A class does not need an __init__ if it has no data to store. Making the object and calling the method is enough.

options: Reuse the attributes and methods of another class
rounds.explain: The child starts with everything the parent has, so the shared code is written once instead of copied.

rounds.prompt: How do you write a class Car that inherits from Vehicle?
rounds.explain: The parent goes in the parentheses. The second option says the opposite, making Vehicle the child.

rounds.prompt: Dog has no eat() of its own. What happens?
options: An error, because Dog has no eat method
rounds.explain: Python does not find eat on Dog, so it looks at the parent and finds it there. Both __init__ and eat were inherited.

rounds.prompt: Both classes define speak(). Which one runs?
options: An error, because the name is used twice
rounds.explain: Python checks the child first and stops as soon as it finds a match, so the child's version overrides the parent's.

rounds.prompt: Build a class that stores a name, make an object from it, and call its method.
rounds.explain: The whole class body comes first, indented under the class line. Only then can you create an object and call a method on it.
